notice: Curated NASA references and historical media. Mission geography, events, resource capacities, timing and scores are educational fiction. Nothing in this bundle is live lunar telemetry.

sources.title: South Pole Illumination Map
sources.summary: Sunlight and deep shadow can be close together near the Moon's south pole. LRO images help scientists study where sunlight reaches the surface.
sources.gameplay_use: Explains why solar generation is valuable and why a route into shadow needs stored energy. The playable map is original fictional terrain.
sources.limitations: This is a historical illumination-map reference, not today's lighting forecast. The publication date is not the observation date; the source combines images collected across six months.

sources.title: Ice on the Moon
sources.organization: NASA / National Space Science Data Center
sources.summary: NASA's LCROSS impact into Cabeus crater helped reveal water-bearing material near the lunar south pole. Very cold shadowed regions can preserve ice.
sources.gameplay_use: Motivates investigating a shadowed science site and collecting a simulated sample.
sources.limitations: The observation date refers to the LCROSS impact. This does not establish ice at every crater, guarantee a playable sample contains ice, or provide a resource concentration for the game's fictional site.

sources.title: What Is a Spacesuit?
sources.summary: A spacesuit's life-support backpack carries oxygen, removes exhaled carbon dioxide, and supplies electricity. Astronauts need these systems while working outside.
sources.gameplay_use: Explains finite oxygen reserves and why longer trips need a safe return plan.
sources.limitations: This reference explains equipment, not a physiological consumption formula. ASTRA oxygen units and equipment bonuses are invented for teaching trade-offs.

sources.title: How NASA Will Protect Astronauts From Space Radiation at the Moon
sources.summary: Energetic particles from the Sun can create a radiation hazard. Mission teams monitor space weather and plan shelter with shielding material.
sources.gameplay_use: Explains the fictional environmental alert and why shelter or ending an excursion can be a sensible choice.
sources.limitations: ASTRA's alert is scripted fiction, not a NASA warning. Its educational radiation-risk index is not absorbed dose, dose equivalent, disease probability, or a real flight limit. Ordinary shadow is not a radiation shelter.
sources.credit: NASA Science Editorial Team / NASA Goddard

sources.title: NASA Image and Video Library: lunar south pole search
sources.summary: NASA's public media catalog provides historical lunar imagery and descriptive metadata. A verified response included the image The Lunar South Pole, NASA ID PIA13523.
sources.gameplay_use: Optional science-explorer media enrichment. Does not affect authoritative mission resources or event timing.
sources.limitations: Search ordering and metadata can change. date_created is catalog media metadata, not necessarily an instrument observation timestamp. A current fetch of an old image is still historical media, not live lunar data.
sources.credit: Per-item NASA center and secondary_creator credits; PIA13523: NASA/GSFC/Arizona State University
